title: The Man Who Wrote the Camps
dek: Russian novelist and historian who exposed the Soviet Gulag.
mortality_event: 1945 arrest, eight years in Soviet labour camps, internal exile, and cancer before the works that exposed the Gulag.
citation_passage: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn (1918–2008) was a Russian writer whose experience of Soviet imprisonment became material for fiction and historical testimony. Arrested in 1945 for criticizing Stalin in private letters, he was sentenced to eight years in labor camps followed by internal exile. One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich, published in 1962, brought camp life into Soviet literature. He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1970. Publication of The Gulag Archipelago in the West was followed by his forced expulsion from the Soviet Union in 1974; he returned to Russia in 1994. This eight-page comic follows imprisonment, survival, and the writing that made the camps a subject of public witness.
